The Quiet Builders — A Community for Devs Who Build with Soul 🌙💻


Not every developer chases trends or applause.
Some of us build in silence.
Some of us write code like poetry.

Some of us launch projects that no one sees — but still matter deeply.
We are the developers who:
Build side-projects late at night
Believe code is art, not just syntax
Create CSS frameworks, languages, ideas — not for fame, but for expression

Work alone, but never without purpose
I’ve been writing, building, and publishing from my heart — including my book, Programming as an Art, and open-source projects like Spider.css and Hinglish.
Sometimes people read.

Sometimes they don’t.

But I never stopped.
This is for all of us who create without claps.

For the devs who vibe with their code — even if no one notices.
It’s not a club. It’s a feeling.
But if you connect with this idea, you can:
Use the tag #thequietbuilders on your posts
Leave a comment below with your story or a project you built quietly
Follow me @pjdeveloper896 — let’s connect as quiet creators
“We don’t make noise. We make meaning.”
If you feel this — welcome home. 🖤

articles.author: Leon Fazliu
articles.description:
Public-facing apps like React, Flutter, or plain JavaScript often make a critical OAuth mistake: they use the Client Credentials Grant to access protected APIs directly from the frontend.
This breaks core OAuth security assumptions.
In this post, I explain:
What the Client Credentials Grant was designed for
Why it’s dangerous to use in public apps
Real-world risks like token leakage and backend impersonation
What to use instead (like PKCE or backend proxies)
The problem is more common than it should be — and it often goes unnoticed until something breaks.
You can read the full breakdown here:

https://blog.sentry.security/oauth-2-0-client-credentials-misuse-in-public-apps/
If you've encountered this or seen similar misuses, feel free to share or discuss below.
articles.title: Misusing OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials in Public Apps — A Security Breakdown

articles.author: Okoye Ndidiamaka
articles.description:
That moment made her realize one thing:
Whether you're a startup founder, software engineer, or tech lead, if you're still deploying manually—you’re wasting time, increasing risk, and slowing innovation.
Enter: CI/CD — Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment.
This isn't just a buzzword. It's the backbone of modern software delivery.
⏱️ What Is CI/CD and Why Should You Care?
Continuous Deployment (CD) takes it a step further by automatically pushing successful builds to production (or staging), making every validated change instantly available to users.
CI/CD removes bottlenecks, minimizes bugs, and accelerates delivery.
💥 Real-World Impact: A Story from the Trenches
Deployments happened once every 2 weeks. Developers dreaded release days. QA was rushed. Bugs slipped through.
After introducing a basic CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions, Docker, and Heroku, everything changed:
Commits triggered automatic tests
Builds were deployed to staging instantly
Releases became boring (as they should be!)
The team went from shipping twice a month to twice a day—with fewer errors.
🔧 Tools to Build Your First CI/CD Pipeline
🔹 GitHub Actions
name: Deploy App
🔹 GitLab CI/CD
🔹 CircleCI / Travis CI
🔹 Docker + Kubernetes
💡 CI/CD Best Practices: Tips That Actually Work
✅ 2. Fail Fast
✅ 3. Use Feature Flags
✅ 4. Secure Your Pipeline
✅ 5. Keep It Fast
🧠 Pro Tip: CI/CD Is Not Just a Dev Tool—It's a Team Culture
Collaboration (smaller, more frequent merges)
Accountability (automated checks catch errors before humans do)
Speed (faster feedback = faster innovation)
Once your team experiences the flow of writing code and seeing it live within minutes—you’ll never go back.
💬 Let’s Talk: How Are You Using CI/CD?
🔁 Final Thoughts: Don’t Fear Automation—Embrace It
The best code in the world is useless if it’s stuck in your local repo.
If you found this helpful, hit the ❤️, share with your dev community, and let’s keep the conversation going.
articles.title: 🚀 From Code to Production in Minutes: Mastering CI/CD for Faster, Smarter Software Delivery
